Rob, that's an astute point about the rounding. That's why the Cholesky solve works in R, but not Stan. You're absolutely right, the non-rounded version should NOT work because it's a 3x3 matrix with rank only equal to 2. 

The reason the rank is only 2 is because it's a linear kernel. So if X is a data matrix with N rows, and D columns, the linear kernel would be X*X^T, which is NxN and has rank at most D. So if D < N the matrix would not be invertible, as was the case with me because I had D=2, N=3. If on the other hand I had a different kernel such as the RBF then D would be uncountably infinite and hence much larger than N, making my kernel invertible. 

This sort of illustrates a hand-wavy way to see why GP's have identifiability issues, as Michael Betancourt has mentioned on here in the past. The "feature-space" is of much higher dimension than the amount of data you have. 

Thank you Daniel and Bob for the debugging tips! I think using the RBF kernel instead of the linear kernel should fix things. I'm going to try that next.
